page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Roots of epiphytes
lines: Epiphytes carry two kinds of specialised
roots: velamen roots and clinging roots.
steps.why: An epiphyte lives on another plant with no contact with soil, so it needs one root system for moisture and another for attachment - two types, both named.
common_mistakes: Naming only velamen roots. The clinging roots are the second half of the answer.
steps.memory_tip: An epiphyte needs to drink and to hold on - velamen drinks, clinging holds.
steps.margin_note: Name both root types plus Vanda as the example.

steps.label: Functions

lines.text: Velamen roots absorb moisture from the

lines: atmosphere through the spongy velamen tissue.
Clinging roots fix the plant to the branches
steps.why: Each root type maps to one function; writing the pair as two matched sentences is what the examiner ticks.
common_mistakes: Writing that epiphyte roots absorb food from the host. An epiphyte only sits on the host; it is not a parasite.
steps.memory_tip: Velamen - vapour from air; clinging - clamped to bark.
steps.margin_note: Two sentences, one per root type - keep the pairing visible.
